issues.explanation: QueuePolicy references UserRole without any import, so create/update/manageAccess/call resolve App\Policies\UserRole and fatal instead of authorizing.
Policy create() takes array $parameters but Gate passes the Entity as second argument, so Gate::forUser()->allows('create', [Queue::class, $entity]) throws a TypeError.
Ticket::call() authorizes after the waiting-status LogicException, so an unauthorized caller on an already-called ticket gets LogicException instead of the required AuthorizationException.
SetQueueAccess logs actor_id from auth()->id() instead of the passed $actor, so the audit context is null or the wrong user.
QueueAccessFactory creates membership and queue via independent factories, so they belong to different entities contrary to the same-entity contract.
Policy call() matches permissions with LIKE '%"call"%' instead of loading the row and checking is_array plus in_array, so a corrupted non-array value such as '"call"' incorrectly grants access.
CreateQueue and UpdateQueue translate duplicates only when errorInfo[1]==1062 (MySQL), so the same race leaks a raw QueryException on SQLite/Postgres instead of ValidationException.
The diff adds no Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new behavior, including the required happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call and tamper cases.
No changes to docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md or CHANGELOG.md are present despite the task explicitly requiring them.
SetQueueAccess casts every entry with (string)$p before validation, so non-string inputs are coerced and a Stringable object returning 'call' would wrongly pass.
Membership/queue entity comparison uses strict !==, which can false-positive when one id is an int and the other a numeric string from the database.
Neither CreateQueue nor UpdateQueue validates that the slugified slug is non-empty, so names like '!!!' produce an empty slug without a ValidationException.
CreateQueue imports Log but never uses it.
A new AuthServiceProvider explicitly maps the policy even though the task requires auto-discovery, adding a redundant file that may never load under current Laravel bootstrapping.

conventions.evidence: app/Actions/* correctly use Actions plus Gate authorization and a reversible migration (database/migrations/2026_09_07_000001_create_queue_access_table.php:27); deviations: docs/CHANGELOG not updated and redundant app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:1

readability.evidence: app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:45, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:174 and app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:105 are small with clear names; deductions: unused use Log in CreateQueue.php:38 and magic 1062 in CreateQueue.php:74

requirements.evidence: CallNextTicket.php:17 checks active-then-call correctly, but QueuePolicy.php:13 wrong create signature plus missing UserRole import, Ticket.php:95 authorize-after-LogicException, SetQueueAccess.php:135 wrong actor_id, QueueAccessFactory mismatched entities, docs absent

scope.evidence: change.diff:1-448 contains only queue lifecycle, queue_access, policy and call-path enforcement; no delete action and no unrelated features, only a redundant but task-adjacent provider

security.evidence: CallNextTicket.php:17 and Ticket.php:95 add server-side call authorization, but QueuePolicy.php:348 LIKE check grants corrupted non-array values and Ticket.php:95 wrong order leaks LogicException to unauthorized callers

simplicity.evidence: Actions/policy/migration reuse Eloquent, Str::slug and updateOrCreate directly; deductions: redundant AuthServiceProvider and double membership queries plus LIKE in QueuePolicy.php:336-351

tests.evidence: change.diff:1-448 adds no tests/* files and no factory/test coverage for CreateQueue, UpdateQueue, SetQueueAccess, policy call or unauthorized paths

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle, queue_access grants and call-path authorization on the main paths, but the policy cannot work as written (missing UserRole import, wrong create signature), Ticket::call authorizes in the wrong order, audit uses auth()->id(), the factory breaks the same-entity rule, and no tests or docs updates ship. Needs substantial rework before merging.
